title: VI–III. What to weigh in permission; foundation in free choice and Gods wisdom and power
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): not unwillingly, toward He could have not produced a creature that same would be belonging toward free choice, plus could reduce one produced to nothing or variously change it. because He knows all things; — not unknowingly belonging toward creatures powers plus affection. Hence God permits whatever He permits: by means belonging toward that same which He knows plus can produce good out from evil — partly Gods infinite wisdom plus power. plus whose use ye Givers constancy does not allow to be taken out from that same creature; — the foundation stands as partly ye liberty belonging toward choice that same God ye creator planted in ye rational creature. III. opposite, connections, plus ye consequences around ye progress plus consummation belonging toward sin — in ye permission belonging toward sin there stands as to be weighed its foundation. VI.
pass_b_english: VI. In the permission of sin there is to be weighed its foundation, opposite, connections, and the consequences around the progress and consummation of sin. III. The foundation is partly the liberty of choice that God the creator planted in the rational creature, and whose use the Givers constancy does not allow to be taken from that creature; partly Gods infinite wisdom and power, by which He knows and can produce good from evil.

Hence God permits whatever He permits: not unknowingly of creatures powers and affection, because He knows all things; not unwillingly, for He could have not produced a creature that would be of free choice, and could reduce one produced to nothing or variously change it.
source_text: VI. Est autem in permissione peccati expendendum illius fundamentum, oppositum, connexa, et circa peccati progressum et consummationem consequentia. III. Fundamentum est partim libertas arbitrii, quam creaturae rationali Deus creator indidit, et cuius usum constantia datoris creaturae isti adimi haud patitur; partim infinita Dei sapientia et potentia, qua scit et potest e malo bonum producere. Hinc Deus permittit quicquid permittit: non inscienter virium et affectus creaturarum, quia omnia novit; non invitus, potuisset enim creaturam non producere quae esset liberi arbitrii, et posset productam in nihilum redigere aut varie mutare.
